title: Introduce lazy request decoding and cooperative event-loop to unblock CPU hotpath
author: Anika Rao
body: Motivation: production p99 CPU consumption spikes traced to eager request deserialization and heavy thread-pin churn in the fast path. On busy hosts the userland work (JSON/proto decode + route lookup + KV cache checks) dominated latency even when the model run time was small. This change reduces CPU overhead by deferring full decode until a handler actually needs structured fields, replacing per-request OS-thread pinning with a cooperative single-threaded event loop for light-weight request dispatch, and reworking the KV cache to per-shard read-mostly paths to avoid a global lock handoff. Summary of changes: 1) Add runtime/serialize/lazy_decoder.rs: a shallow header parse that extracts only routing keys and request sizes, and a thin accessor that decodes fields on first access. 2) Introduce runtime/dispatch/event_loop.rs: a cooperative event loop that handles socket read, shallow parse, routing, and small-scope scheduling decisions; long-running or kernel-intensive work is submitted to a short-lived worker pool via a lock-free handoff queue. 3) Rework KV cache in runtime/kv/cache_shard.rs to use epoch-based fast reads and an update path that copies-on-write for rare mutations to keep fast path lockless. 4) Continuous batching change in runtime/batching/coalesce.rs: cancel-less deadline batching that opportunistically coalesces requests without blocking the event loop and uses a soft backpressure signal to avoid head-of-line blocking. 5) Add microbench and e2e perf tests: tests/perf/lazy_decode_bench.py and tests/e2e/dispatch_smoke_test.go. Results: internal perf runs show median CPU user-time per request reduced by ~28%, 95th latency improved by ~18% and p99 improved by ~34% on our small-sequence LLM workload (same hardware and traffic replay). Checklist: [x] perf benchmarks added and scripted for CI replay, [x] unit tests for lazy decoder and KV shard, [x] integration smoke test for dispatch/event loop, [x] canary rollout plan included in docs/perf/notes.md. Backwards compatibility: runtime API and public wire formats unchanged; lazy decode is strictly internal and transparent. Risks & mitigations: deferring decode could change when decoding errors surface—decoder is now hermetic and always raises a typed decode error during handler evaluation; added metric runtime.request.decode_late_count to monitor. The event loop reduces OS thread migrations but requires careful yield points; added watchdogs and a cooperative-yield metric to ensure fairness. Rollout plan: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%) with a short hold after each step for perf/regressions. Related: ENG-1423 (CPU hotpath profiling), ENG-1498 (KV cache contention investigation).
commits: KV shard: epoch reads + copy-on-write updates
Batching: deadline coalescer and soft backpressure
Fix: address race in cache updates
changed_files: runtime/serialize/lazy_decoder.rs: new file, adds shallow parse API and lazy field accessors
runtime/dispatch/event_loop.rs: new file, cooperative event loop + dispatcher
runtime/dispatch/worker_pool.rs: adapt to lock-free handoff queue and lifecycle changes
runtime/kv/cache_shard.rs: rework to epoch-based reads and COW updates
runtime/batching/coalesce.rs: replace blocking aggregator with deadline-based coalescer
runtime/metrics/dispatch_metrics.rs: add decode_late_count and yield metrics
docs/perf/notes.md: canary plan and perf comparison charts
ci/bench/replay_config.yaml: new replay config for CI perf runs
reviews: Miguel Santos (Reviewer): Overall this looks like the right direction. A few concerns: the epoch sequence for KV reads needs comments about memory growth and the backpressure signal may under-react on tail-CPU bursts. Please add a small explanation and one more test for GC of epochs.
Anika Rao (Author): Thanks Miguel, added comments in cache_shard.rs and a unit test 'epoch_gc_test' that forces churn; documented memory bounds in docs/perf/notes.md.

Eleanor Kim (Reviewer): I ran the perf replay on my m-class hosts. P99 improvement matches your numbers but I saw a small increase in 50ms allocations from the worker handoff path. Can we reduce allocations on the queue path?

Anika Rao (Author): Reworked the handoff queue to reuse a pooled node and removed an extra boxed closure — new commit 'Perf tweaks: reduce allocation churn' addresses this. Reran the replay and allocations at 50ms bucket are down.
Jared Bloom (Approver): Tested canary stage and verified no increase in error rates and improved tail latency. Approving to merge.
CI Bot: linux-build passed, unit-tests passed, perf-replay passed (baseline comparison attached).
release_notes: Reduced CPU user-time on request hotpath by deferring decode and using a cooperative dispatch loop; p99 latency and throughput improvements for small-sequence workloads. See docs/perf/notes.md for numbers and canary plan.
notes: Canary rollout completed on 2024-10-15 without incidents
